articles.title: Netflix is making a big bet on video podcasts
articles.summary: Netflix is taking a dive into video podcasts through a new partnership with Spotify that will bring 16 shows to the streaming service, including The Bill Simmons Podcast and Conspiracy Theories.
articles.body: Netflix is no longer just a home for TV shows, movies, documentaries, and live WWE matches — soon, you’ll be able to stream video podcasts, too. The streaming giant announced on Tuesday that it’s partnering with Spotify’s podcast studio and The Ringer to offer 16 series on its platform, including The Bill Simmons Podcast, Conspiracy Theories, as well as The Ringer’s shows on the NFL, NBA, Fantasy Football, and F1. The podcasts will appear on Netflix in the US starting in 2026 before expanding to other countries. As part of the deal, the shows won’t appear “in their entirety” on YouTube, according to a report from The New York Times. Not only is YouTube Netflix’s biggest rival, it also tops Spotify and Apple Music as the most popular podcast streaming platform, raking in more than 1 billion listeners each month. Video podcasts, which show hosts during their conversations, are becoming increasingly popular as creators try to expand their reach across social media. Netflix won’t show commercial breaks for this first round of video podcasts, but Spotify’s ads within the podcasts will remain, the Times reports. The streaming service already produces several podcasts about its shows, like You Cannot Make This Up, Skip Intro, and We Have the Receipts, which also appear on YouTube. In April, Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos hinted at bringing podcasts to the platform during an earnings call, saying, “As the popularity of video podcasts grow, I suspect you’ll see some of them find their way to Netflix.” It sounds like Spotify has more plans to expand the reach of its podcasts, too, as the company says it aims to “bring similar opportunities to a wider range of creators” in the future. You can view the full list of podcasts coming to Netflix on the company’s website.

articles.title: Netflix is using an AI-generated Gene Wilder voice in its Willy Wonka reality show
articles.summary: Wonka’s The Golden Ticket will premiere September 23rd on Netflix, with Gene Wilder’s AI-recreated voice as part of the show.
articles.body: A new teaser trailer confirmed that Wonka’s The Golden Ticket will premiere on Netflix on September 23rd, following its Squid Game reality show in the trend of creating real competitions based on fictional torture scenarios. While the sets seen in the trailer are real and not some Glasgow-style AI fakes, the voiceover is AI-generated. Deadline reports that Netflix worked with AI audio company ElevenLabs with consent from Wilder’s family, after working on productions re-creating the voice of Michael Caine and Stan Lee. It also continues Netflix’s 2021 partnership with the Roald Dahl company, and is separate from the Charlie vs. the Chocolate Factory animated feature that will arrive in 2027. As for the show itself, Netflix says its “high-stakes social experiment” will feature 12 “lucky” golden ticket winners plus their chosen partner in the competition, with one champion left standing a week later during the two-part finale on September 30th.

articles.title: ABC sues the FCC over Trump and Carr’s campaign of threats
articles.summary: ABC is suing the Federal Communications Commission over claims that the agency “waged a retaliatory campaign” against its networks over their political coverage.
articles.body: ABC is suing the Federal Communications Commission over claims the agency “waged a retaliatory campaign” against its networks over the content they broadcast. In a lawsuit filed in federal court on Tuesday, ABC and its parent company Disney accuse the FCC of “punishing ABC for its speech” by threatening its broadcast licenses. It’s the latest escalation in the dispute between ABC and the Trump administration, which has been critical of the network’s political coverage — especially by late-night host Jimmy Kimmel and The View. The FCC opened an investigation into The View’s airtime of political candidates in February and ordered ABC stations owned by Disney to file for an early license renewal in April. ABC fired back with a series of letters slamming the FCC’s decision, claiming it will chill free speech. It also didn’t broadcast President Donald Trump’s July 16th speech on its linear channels and streamed it on ABC News Live instead. ABC’s lawsuit alleges the Trump administration has “steadily increased the pressure” on its networks over the past several months, claiming the latest attack on its broadcast licenses “underscores the Commission’s true purpose: coercing and retaliating against a network that refuses to bow to the Administration’s demands.” Bloomberg reported in July that the FCC could take action against ABC and Disney as soon as this month. ABC and Disney are seeking a court order halting the FCC’s broadcast license renewal proceedings. In a statement to CNBC, an FCC spokesperson says, “Disney is obviously very concerned about the FCC’s proceeding, as evidenced by their ongoing campaign of disinformation as well as their decision to ask a court to stop the FCC from further pursuing matters.” The FCC will “continue to follow the facts and law wherever they lead,” the spokesperson adds. “The consequences of the Administration’s campaign against free speech reach well beyond ABC,” ABC’s lawsuit claims. “If the Administration gets its way, the message to every media company in the country will be unmistakable: tell only the stories the Administration deems favorable, or face the coercive machinery of the federal government. In such a world, the press could in no way be described as free.” Update, August 18th: Added a statement from the FCC.

articles.title: FBI raided Swalwell’s home, seized devices as part of sexual assault probe
articles.summary: Correction: The FBI raid of Swalwell’s home was related to sexual assault allegations. An earlier story included incorrect information. Updated at 12:18 p.m. EDT The FBI reportedly raided former Rep. Eric Swalwell’s (D-Calif.) home and confiscated his electronic devices over the weekend amid an ongoing probe, according to multiple outlets. The FBI searched the former congressman’s…
articles.body:
Correction: The FBI raid of Swalwell’s home was related to sexual assault allegations. An earlier story included incorrect information. Updated at 12:18 p.m. EDT

The FBI reportedly raided former Rep. Eric Swalwell’s (D-Calif.) home and confiscated his electronic devices over the weekend amid an ongoing probe , according to multiple outlets.

The FBI searched the former congressman’s home in Washington, D.C., Sunday after they seized devices from Swalwell in San Francisco on Saturday, per The New York Times. The probe concerns allegations of sexual assault, the newspaper reported.

The raid comes just days after news broke of Swalwell’s “physical relations” with Christine Fang, a suspected Chinese spy, as outlined in newly declassified documents released by the White House Government Transparency Task Force. The FBI had previously investigated Fang.

Allegations of sexual assault are ultimately what led Swalwell to suspend his campaign for California’s governorship and resign from his House seat in April. Swalwell has denied any wrongdoing.

Swalwell was accused of assaulting a Capitol Hill staffer — who was 17 years his junior — twice in the midst of his current marriage, as initially reported by the San Francisco Chronicle .

The former House Democrat is being investigated by the FBI, Manhattan district attorney’s office and the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department over the allegations that surfaced this spring.

In the Chinese spy probe, as revealed in the documents released earlier this week, Swalwell said he met Fang in 2015 and had “physical relations” with her on a “handful of occasions but never dated her or had a romantic relationship.”

Federal investigators determined she ran a political intelligence gathering operation directed by China’s primary civilian spy agency between 2011 and 2015.

An independent journalistic probe revealed that her objective was to infiltrate U.S. political circles to gather unclassified but sensitive political intelligence, manipulate campaign financing, and cultivate relationships with up-and-coming politicians who had national potential, as reported by Axios .

FBI memos show that Fang facilitated an illicit scheme to route campaign donations through straw donors.

In at least two cases, she used American conduits to obscure the fact that the political contributions were secretly being funded by the Chinese government.

Federal investigators also uncovered evidence that Fang placed Chinese nationals and foreign interns inside Swalwell’s congressional office in exchange for campaign fundraising support.

articles.title: Twitch and Amazon face lawsuit over use of streamers' content to train AI
articles.summary: The lawsuit alleges Twitch used streamers' videos to train AI without their permission or proper compensation.
articles.body:
Amazon is facing a lawsuit over its move to train its AI models on videos people broadcast on the popular streaming platform Twitch.

The move faced backlash from users when it was announced in August - with people having the option to opt-out if they do not want their data used this way.

The class action lawsuit has been brought on behalf of millions of streamers who use Twitch, alleging its parent company Amazon used their videos to train AI without their permission or proper compensation.

Twitch and Amazon have not commented on the lawsuit.

Streamers on the platform reportedly produced more than 215 million hours of content in the first few months of 2026 alone.

The lawsuit was brought by Connecticut-based streamer Warren Pandiscia.

It claims Twitch breached its contract with users by using that content as AI training data for Amazon's models without obtaining their permission.

It adds streamers should not have their work commercially exploited to develop AI without consent or compensation.

The lawsuit seeks damages for streamers whose content was allegedly used to train AI, as well as an order preventing Amazon from continuing the alleged practice.

It is not clear when Amazon began collecting Twitch users' data to train its AI models.

Twitch's chief product officer Mike Minton previously said he did not know if users' data had been scraped for training before it gave people the opportunity to opt-out.

He said he was unsure what Amazon "has done in terms of model training and what they've used and not used".

In Twitch's own FAQs about AI training, it said a person's audio might be used to "refine models that create speech to text".

It said this would help improve automatic subtitles on Twitch streams as well as Amazon videos.

Those that want to disable the feature would need to navigate to the Settings tab in their Streamer Dashboard, click the Security and Privacy tab, then scroll down to near the bottom of the options and toggle off "training for Generative AI".

However, the opt-out only applies to individual streams, meaning creators' content could still be used for AI training when they appear in a stream where the feature remains enabled.

Amazon, which bought Twitch for nearly $1bn (£740m) in 2014, has made AI a major focus as it competes with Google, Meta and other tech giants.

articles.title: Netflix reportedly considers opening its app to other streamers
articles.summary: Executives discussed making Peacock and Fox One available through the Netflix app, The New York Times reports.
articles.body: Netflix executives have considered making third-party streaming services available within its app, according to a report from The New York Times. The recent discussions reportedly centered around bringing Peacock and Fox One to Netflix, though it’s unclear whether the streaming giant would sell subscriptions to the other services or add their content to its app. While Amazon’s Prime Video and Roku have long sold subscriptions to rival services, the move would be a major change for Netflix, which has only joined bundles with other streamers. YouTube — Netflix’s biggest rival — will also include access to Peacock as part of its Premium subscription next year. Netflix currently has no “imminent deal” planned, The New York Times reports. But Netflix has already begun dabbling in third-party streaming partnerships in France, where it folded live channels and streaming content from local broadcaster TF1 into its app in June. When asked about this partnership during a July earnings call, Netflix co-CEO Greg Peters said the company is seeing “promising” results. “If we see additional deals that similarly serve our members that work for our partner, that work for us, we’ll certainly consider them,” Peters said. Netflix declined to comment. Update, August 24th: Added Netflix’s response.

articles.title: ESPN streaming plans are getting more expensive
articles.summary: ESPN is raising prices across its plans, with the ad-supported Select tier going from $12.99 to $13.99 per month, and its Unlimited plan increasing from $29.99 to $31.99 per month.
articles.body: ESPN is hiking the price of its subscription on September 17th, a change that will also impact its bundles with Disney Plus. In a support page spotted earlier by Sports Media Watch, ESPN says its ad-supported Select membership will cost $13.99 instead of $12.99 / month, while its Unlimited plan will rise to $31.99 from $29.99 / month. The annual ESPN Select plan is also going to $139.99 from $129.99 / year, and the annual Unlimited tier is increasing to $319.99 from $299.99 / year. Meanwhile, Disney Plus bundles with ESPN Select are going up in price as well. Here’s a rundown of the changes: * Disney Plus (with ads), Hulu (with ads), and ESPN Select: $21.99 / month, up from $19.99 / month. * Disney Plus (ad-free), Hulu (ad-free), ESPN Select: $32.99 / month, up from $29.99. * Legacy Disney Plus (ad-free), Hulu (ad-free), and ESPN Select: $27.99 / month, up from $24.99 / month. Disney Plus bundles with ESPN Unlimited aren’t affected. Last week, Axios reported that about 80 percent of Unlimited subscribers signed up through the bundle with Disney Plus and Hulu. Though Disney last raised prices across its bundles last year, this is the first increase for ESPN, which rolled out its standalone streaming subscription last August. As part of the launch, ESPN updated its mobile app with a TikTok-like feed of videos and a personalized version of SportsCenter. ESPN also launched multiview in its app on major smart TV platforms.

articles.title: Amazon and Twitch Face Class-Action Lawsuit After Introducing Opt-Out Setting That Uses Streamers' Content to Train AI
articles.summary: Twitch and Amazon are facing a class-action lawsuit after the streaming platform rolled out a feature that automatically trains its generative AI on streamers’ content unless they opt out.
articles.body:
Twitch and Amazon are facing a class-action lawsuit after the streaming platform rolled out a feature that automatically trains its generative AI on streamers’ content unless they manually opt out.

The setting sparked a wave of backlash when it was rolled out last week. "Allow your channel content to train generative AI content models at Amazon," it reads.

It’s buried in users’ security and privacy settings, and is automatically turned on by default. Streamers must toggle the option off in order to opt out of it — but that doesn’t stop Twitch from using their channel content for other purposes, as outlined in the platform’s Privacy Notice .

We've added a setting that lets you opt out of having your channel content used to train generative AI content models across Amazon. Click here to learn more: — Twitch Support (@TwitchSupport) August 12, 2026

We've added a setting that lets you opt out of having your channel content used to train generative AI content models across Amazon. Click here to learn more:

Just a week later, Amazon and Twitch were officially named in a class-action lawsuit filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California on August 20, 2026. In the 37-page complaint, plaintiff Warren Pandiscia — a Twitch streamer based in Connecticut with over 900 followers — argues that Amazon “unlawfully” scraped creators’ content without their consent by automatically opting them into the AI training setting.

“Defendants’ actions were not only unlawful, but an unconscionable attack on the community of content creators whose content is used to fuel the multitrillion-dollar generative AI industry without any compensation," the suit reads.

"Content creators such as Plaintiff and the Class Members will never be able to claw back the intellectual property unlawfully copied and used by Defendants to train Amazon’s generative AI. Once AI ingests content, that content is stored in its neural network, and not capable of deletion or retraction. Defendants’ actions constitute abuse and exploitation of content creators’ work for Defendants’ profit."

Damages sought include “all available contract damages, including actual, compensatory, consequential, and nominal damages, together with such other relief as the Court deems just and proper,” though no specific monetary amount was mentioned.

Twitch, for its part, has defended its stance on automatically opting creators into Amazon’s AI training. During a ‘Patch Notes’ stream that was broadcast that same day, Twitch's chief product officer Mike Minton responded to questions about the setting, saying plainly: “If it was opt-in, nobody would opt in. That’s honestly the answer.”

Twitch’s Account Settings FAQ explains that it trains Amazon’s generative AI on users’ content for things like “[refining] models that create speech to text, which would help improve captions at Twitch but would also help improve captions across Amazon,” and “AI-supported features, like captions, which automatically generate captions for your Clips but does not retain your stream or your clips to train a model that can generate new content.”

Twitch has not provided an official comment on the lawsuit at the time of writing. IGN has reached out for comment.

articles.title: Democrat rips Hasan Piker as 'hack who thrives on hate' over his warning to American Jews about Israel
articles.summary: Rep. Hillary Scholten condemned Hasan Piker's remarks about American Jews and Israel, calling the Twitch streamer a "hack who thrives on hate."
articles.body: Controversial far-left Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, who has become increasingly prominent in Democratic politics, is facing backlash from Rep. Hillary Scholten, D-Mich., over his remarks about American Jews' support for Israel that she characterized as "talk of violence" targeting Jewish Michigan state Sen. Jeremy Moss. In a statement published Monday, Scholten said Piker was "a hack who thrives on hate, shock and awe because he lacks substance." "Hasan Piker's talk of violence against American Jews, and directly naming a Michigan elected official, and future member of Congress, Jeremy Moss, is unacceptable. Full stop," Scholten's statement read. "We should all be calling out this disgusting rhetoric so it loses its grip on our politics once and for all. It has no place in Michigan, and no place in our country." HASAN PIKER IS BECOMING THE 'FACE OF THE PROGRESSIVE MOVEMENT,' FORMER DEMOCRATIC OPERATIVE WARNS In his response to Scholten's statement, Piker called Scholten an "Israel 1st congresswoman." "if i was an israel 1st congresswoman with a possible cheating scandal with a republican in the state, i wouldn’t spend so much time vying for the spotlight by actively defaming a prominent antizionist voice to harm the dem senate majority chances over a 90/10 issue," Piker wrote on X. Piker, who holds a large social media following, has been particularly visible in Michigan this election cycle. He backed Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, who defeated Rep. Haley Stevens in a primary earlier this month. El-Sayed was criticized for appearing with Piker during his campaign, with some saying that the streamer's rhetoric was too extreme. Scholten backed Stevens last month, calling her a "smart, capable, and common-sense leader." She later praised Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer for endorsing Stevens. El-Sayed also responded to Piker's comments, and while he did not condemn the streamer outright, he denounced antisemitism and rhetoric that puts the Jewish community in danger. "I believe all Americans deserve the right to advocate for what they believe without fear of violence. This is particularly true for communities that have been intimidated for their beliefs in the past," El-Sayed wrote. "My commitment to Jewish safety is the same as my commitment to the safety of my own daughters," he added. "Antisemitism is a scourge, and we need to address it in all its forms. And I stand against any rhetoric that puts the community at risk." EL-SAYED DISAVOWS HASAN PIKER'S 9/11 COMMENTS BUT DECRIES 'CANCEL CULTURE' In his statement, El-Sayed stressed that Piker did not speak for his campaign, writing that, "nobody speaks for this campaign besides me and my campaign spokespeople." In addition to politicians, Piker was also criticized by Jewish organizations.  In a statement to Fox News Digital, the Jewish Federation of Detroit said that "Hasan Piker’s talk of violence against Jewish Americans while displaying a picture of a Michigan lawmaker who is Jewish is repugnant and antisemitic." "We call on all responsible leaders to condemn this extremist, attention-seeking conduct which divides Americans, foments hate, and makes our Jewish community less safe," the Jewish Federation of Detroit's statement read. The American Jewish Committee (AJC) also said on Monday that by using an image of Moss, "Piker put a target on the backs of Sen. Moss, Jewish candidates and officeholders, and American Jews alike." "Blaming Jews for the antisemitism directed at them is itself antisemitism," AJC wrote on X. "Every public official who has shared his platform now has a choice: denounce this and walk away, or be complicit. There is no third option." Anti-Defamation League CEO Jonathan Greenblatt weighed in as well, questioning whether elected officials who associate with Piker really watch his streams or if "they just see his reach and ignore the rampant antisemitism." "The Jewsplaining is extraordinary: Piker appoints himself an authority on antisemitism, lecturing Jews about what is and isn’t antisemitic while blaming the Jewish community for the hatred directed against it," Greenblatt said of Piker. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE During his Aug. 20 stream, Piker seemed to warn American Jews against supporting Israel, saying that doing so could lead to violence against them. "People don't f--- with Israel any longer. And if Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they're singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone will come around and take action not against Israel, mind you, but against American Jews," Piker said. When he made the comment, Piker had an image of Moss, who is running to fill Stevens' seat, in his background. Piker's remarks came amid a controversy over an audio clip circulating online in which Moss purportedly said that the "entire purpose" of his congressional campaign was to ensure America's continued support for Israel. However, the Michigan Democrat said that the clip was fabricated, calling it "a manipulated and unsourced audio, with things I never did and never would say." "We are in a dangerous era of disinformation. Circulating a lie because it affirms your bias or belief is equally bad whether it comes from the left or the right. We all have a choice not to spread fabricated images, videos, and audio about candidates and campaigns. We all have a role in stopping the erosion of our democracy," Moss said about the controversy over the audio clip. articles.title: Instagram’s ‘First Draft’ trims your Reels clips for you
articles.summary: Instagram is rolling out a new Reels-editing feature that automatically trims your clips to make them ready to share.
articles.body: Instagram is launching a new Reels-editing feature that automatically trims your video clips to focus on the highlights. The feature, called First Draft, is rolling out to Instagram’s iPhone app and provides a “starting point” that you can build upon with other edits, according to an announcement on Tuesday. An example shared by Instagram shows a user selecting multiple clips for a reel and then tapping the “First Draft” button. From there, Instagram analyzes the clips — each of which is more than a minute long — before trimming them down to eliminate pauses and showcase the most important parts. Instagram then combines the snippets into a reel that’s ready to edit and share. [Video: Instagram First Draft] It sounds similar to Adobe’s AI-powered Quick Cut feature, which automatically combines clips based on a prompt. But unlike Adobe’s feature, Instagram’s First Draft tool doesn’t use AI, according to Instagram spokesperson Nicole Rechtszaid. Instagram says First Draft works with “multi-clip montages, talking-head videos, and day-in-the-life content.” You can find the feature by opening the camera app in Instagram, filming your video, and tapping the First Draft Button. You can also find it in your Reels gallery after selecting more than one clip. Update, August 25th: Added confirmation that First Draft doesn’t use AI.

articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed distances from Hasan Piker — kind of
articles.summary: Is Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed distancing himself from controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker? That’s the headline, but it’s not quite true.
articles.body:
Is Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed distancing himself from controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker? That’s the headline, but it’s not quite true. I’d say it’s a tepid distancing at best. Itty bitty distancing.

First, Hasan Piker made some truly awful (but entirely characteristic) comments about how Jewish people are really sort of just asking for it with those whole supporting Israel thing — sooner or later, somebody’s going to do something bad to the Jews because they like Israel. Seriously, that’s the gist of what he said .

Now, those comments were specifically aimed at Jeremy Moss, a Michigan state senator and Democrat who has been reluctant to endorse El-Sayed due to his proximity to the relentless Israel critic. And they’re truly vile sentiments. In the first place, likening the state of Israel to ISIS is simply ridiculous. Again, for the thousandth time, it’s fine to criticize Israel or disagree with its government or think that it’s caused too much destruction in Gaza. But you’re living in a delusion if you think Israel is like ISIS only Jewish.

Piker is living in that delusion though, and he thinks it’s so obvious that Israel is ISIS levels of bad that someone, I guess, is going to come along and hurt Jewish people unless they really turn on Israel.

I should note that this is already happening: There is rising antisemitism on both the left and the right and, yes, it’s partly because Israel’s popularity has declined. It’s one thing to recognize that fact, and it’s quite another to imply — as Hasan Piker assuredly did — that the Jews basically deserve it unless they disassociate from Israel entirely. It’s basically very similar to the discourse around America deserving 9/11 , one of Piker’s earlier controversial remarks.

But Piker was also directing this comment at Moss very significantly, including by sharing a picture of him. What he’s implying is, denounce Israel or else who knows what’s going to happen. Something very bad.

And he’s been called out for it by Democrats, including Rep. Hillary Scholten .

Scholten has also been reluctant to endorse El-Sayed. So El-Sayed, who campaigned alongside Piker and chose him to be a surrogate and spokesperson, is finally speaking up — sort of. El-Sayed put out a statement that he claimed was aimed at Piker’s comments about Moss, although he doesn’t mention either of them in the statement. He writes:

“I believe all Americans deserve the right to advocate for what they believe without fear of violence. This is particularly true for communities that have been intimidated for their beliefs in the past. My commitment to Jewish safety is the same as my commitment to the safety of my own daughters. Antisemitism is a scourge, and we need to address it in all its forms. And I stand against any rhetoric that puts the community at risk. But I want to be crystal clear, nobody speaks for this campaign besides me and my campaign spokespeople.”

OK, but El-Sayed clearly tried to cash in on Piker’s star power by associating with him. If he now wants to disassociate, he’s got to say it more explicitly than that.

What’s really happening is that El-Sayed can read polling data, and he’s concerned he could actually blow this race, even in a political environment that’s maximally unfriendly for Republicans. So he’s distancing himself ever so slightly.

Of course, I suspect El-Sayed might actually agree with the spirit of what Piker said. In fact, when Temple Israel in West Bloomfield, Mich., was attacked by a deranged man, an Arab American who had lost family members in Lebanon, El-Sayed said repeatedly, “hurt people hurt people.”

That’s probably why some Jewish Michiganders are having trouble supporting him. Because they don’t see a tremendous amount of distance between Hasan Piker and Abdul El-Sayed.

And some Democrats understand that this is a problem, even very progressive ones. Activist Cameron Kasky wrote on X : “Hasan Piker is absolutely a ‘problem’ for Democrats. Centrists are attacking our party over him instead of the authoritarianism and corruption unfolding literally right before our eyes.

“Republicans are laughing about it,” he continues. “We are fabricating an electoral weakness out of thin air.”

Robby Soave is co-host of The Hill’s commentary show “Rising” and a senior editor for Reason Magazine. This column is an edited transcription of his daily commentary.

articles.title: Tech stocks today: Meta agrees to settle social media case for $16.68 billion
articles.summary: This week's major tech news
articles.body: Meta (META) agreed to settle a social media addiction case with a group of state attorneys general on Wednesday, putting an end to the trial in its second week. The stock initially popped on the news before paring gains.The case revolved around allegations from 29 states that Instagram and Facebook developed products to hook young users on the platforms and harvested the data of children under 13 to their benefit.According to court filings, Meta denied wrongdoing and agreed to pay up to $16.68 billion.In a statement on the company's website, Meta said, "Ensuring teens have a safe and productive experience on our platforms is an absolute imperative for Meta. We want to get this right for parents and teens, and that's why we partnered with state attorneys general to set a new industry standard."According to DC Attorney General Brian L. Schwalb, these are among the safety features Meta has agreed to implement:Hard cap daily time limits and "Productive Pauses" for children on its two platforms, Instagram and Facebook. Meta will adopt a combined two-hour daily time limit with mandatory pauses after 15 minutes of continuous use and again at 60 and 90 minutes to interrupt endless scrolling. These limits remain in effect for five years. If Snapchat, TikTok, and YouTube adopt comparable terms, the daily limit on each platform will drop to 60 minutes for 10 years."Nighttime blocks" restricting children's access to feeds from 12:00 a.m. to 6:00 a.m and silencing notifications from 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.Limited school-time access for children, eliminating push notifications on weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. during the school year.Strict age verification measures and safer, age-appropriate content controls, including stronger safeguards against bullying, content promoting eating disorders, and content related to suicide and self-harm.Stronger, more user-friendly parental controls.Limits on social comparison features, including beauty filters and visible "like" counts that have been linked to poor mental health outcomes for kids.Regular assessment by an independent auditor of the implementation and efficacy of the safety features, with oversight by the settling states.Nvidia earnings on tapMeta isn't the only tech giant making headlines. Another key moment for Wall Street is due to arrive after the bell on Wednesday: Nvidia's (NVDA) second quarter earnings.While its Big Tech peers reported their results nearly a month ago, Nvidia is finally giving us the lowdown on its latest quarter when it reports Q2 earnings after the close on Wednesday.For the quarter, Nvidia is expected to report second quarter adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $2.09 on revenue of $92 billion, according to Bloomberg analyst consensus estimates. That would mark a 96% year-over-year jump in overall revenue, and a continued quarter-over-quarter acceleration.

articles.title: Spotify launches Premium Early Access in India, Badshah and Harrdy Sandhu among first releases
articles.summary: Tech News News: Music streaming app Spotify has launched Premium Early Access in India, allowing Premium subscribers to listen to select new music releases up to thre.
articles.body: Music streaming app Spotify has launched Premium Early Access in India, allowing Premium subscribers to listen to select new music releases up to three days before they become available to everyone else. The feature will be available from August 28. As announced by the company, Universal Music Group (UMG) will be the first label to launch its ‘Hear It First’ campaign under the new framework. After the early access window ends, the releases will be available to all Spotify listeners. Spotify said no music will be permanently held back.Among the first local releases is Badshah and Divya Kumar's new single ‘Chimna’, which will be available to Premium subscribers on August 28. The song will be available to all listeners on August 31.Harrdy Sandhu's new single ‘Stuck On You’ is also part of the first wave of releases. It will be available to Premium subscribers from August 28 and to all listeners from August 31.Spotify said more local and international artists will be added to the programme in the coming weeks.Premium Early Access will be available to users on Spotify Premium Standard, Premium Platinum and Premium Student plans in India. Eligible releases will appear automatically in users' feeds, with no action required from subscribers.Spotify Free users will be able to listen to every Premium Early Access release once the early access window ends. The company said users who want earlier access can subscribe to a Premium plan.The feature will only apply to releases where artists and their labels have collaborated with Spotify to participate in the programme. Spotify said not all new releases will have an early access window.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: A streamer once promised to stay live while people kept subscribing; 31 days later, he finally switched the camera off
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Subathons are not new in the streaming community. A lot of streamers use subathons to gain traction and subscribers. However, one streamer’s subathon .
articles.body: Subathons are not new in the streaming community. A lot of streamers use subathons to gain traction and subscribers. However, one streamer’s subathon lasted for 31 days. The streamer we’re talking about is Ludwig Ahgren. The wildest part of Ludwig Ahgren’s famous Twitch stunt was not that he planned to stream for a month. He did not. When the broadcast started in March 2021, Ludwig expected the whole thing to last around 24 to 48 hours. Instead, a tiny countdown became the reason he remained live for 31 days. By the time he finally switched the camera off on April 13, 2021, the stream had reached 282,191 active paying subscribers. That number pushed him past Tyler “Ninja” Blevins’ 2018 Twitch record of 269,154. The stunt also brought in an estimated $1.4 million in gross revenue.A 30-minute timer was all it took to keep the stream aliveLudwig started with a 30-minute clock. Viewers could add time by buying a Tier 1 subscription or gifting one, with each subscription putting another 10 to 20 seconds onto the countdown. The idea looked simple, but it created a loop that was hard to stop.People kept gifting. The clock kept moving. Zero never came. Ludwig had expected the experiment to end after a day or two. Instead, the community kept the timer alive again and again, turning a short challenge into a continuous broadcast that lasted more than 740 hours.Sleeping, showering and moderating all became part of the showOnce the stream stretched into weeks, there was no neat separation between “content” and normal life. Ludwig slept on a custom racecar bed while viewers watched. His sleep periods made up roughly a third of the broadcast, while his moderators filled those hours with movie nights, reactions and chat games.Even a shower became part of the livestream. Ludwig wore shorts and used a privacy curtain so the setup stayed within Twitch’s rules.There was also a money-safety measure built into the event. Ludwig capped gifted subscriptions at 100 per account and banned viewers who tried to get around that limit. The goal was to stop individual fans from spending huge amounts simply to keep the stream running.The record was huge, but the payout looked very differentThe final subscriber count was historic, but gross revenue did not equal personal earnings. From the estimated $1.4 million, Twitch took a 50% share. Ludwig also had major expenses, including moderator wages and taxes.He donated a significant amount to St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital and the Humane Society too. After all those costs, his personal share was estimated at about $200,000.The stream ended because Ludwig eventually added a hard 31-day limit. On April 13, the countdown hit zero, and the camera finally went dark.The subathon then became a launchpad for what came next. Months later, Ludwig left Twitch after signing an exclusive, multi-million dollar live-streaming deal with YouTube Gaming. His month-long experiment had ended, but its impact on his career clearly did not stop there. The deal also ended his Twitch tenure.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Fiorella é uma pequena borboleta de três anteninhas que ainda não sabia voar, mas, com o apoio da família e dos amigos, aprende a acreditar em si mesma e a conviver com suas particularidades. Ambientada em um jardim encantado e povoada por personagens como a Mariposa Bruxa, a Rainha das Fadas e a Esperança, a obra é uma metáfora sensível sobre a síndrome de Down (Trissomia do 21).

A proposta é transformar a pista em uma grande biblioteca viva, onde livros, memórias e diferentes fases da vida ganham movimento por meio da patinação artística. A história começa com um senhor de cabelos brancos, cercado por fotografias, medalhas e troféus, que revisita sua trajetória a partir de duas grandes paixões: a literatura e a patinação.

articles.title: Apple TV now costs $14.99 a month after its fourth price hike in four years
articles.summary: Apple TV is going up in price, with the monthly subscription going from $12.99 to $14.99 per month.
articles.body: Apple raised the price of its streaming service for new and current subscribers on Friday, bumping it up from $12.99 per month to $14.99, Deadline and Variety are reporting. An annual subscription now costs $119, up from $99. Apple also increased the cost of its individual Apple One subscription, which includes Apple TV and Apple’s other subscription services, from $19.95 per month to $21.95. According to Deadline and Variety, the price change is effective immediately, and current subscribers will be notified of it before their next bill. This price hike comes almost exactly a year after Apple last increased its Apple TV subscription fee. It comes just weeks after Apple premiered the fourth season of Ted Lasso, and has increasingly aired live sports like F1, MLB, and Major League Soccer in addition to its prestige TV shows and original movies. Earlier this year, Apple also raised prices on almost all of its devices, and is reportedly planning to increase AppleCare Plus subscription prices.

articles.title: WWE SmackDown results, grades (Aug. 28): Sami Zayn stands tall after chaos reigns in main event
articles.summary: "WWE SmackDown" took over Ottawa tonight for the big Undisputed WWE Championship No. 1 contender match between Kevin Owens, Gunther and Finn Balor.
articles.body: WWE stayed in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada on this Friday — August 28 — for the latest "WWE SmackDown," following up last week's big CM Punk vs. Kevin Owens world title match. To say that this iteration of the show missed the mark would be an understatement.KO'ing the audienceDespite WWE's planned pre-tapings of "SmackDown" for the next two weeks, it still felt like there had to be a significant follow-up to one of the biggest TV matches of the company's year, right?Wrong. Entirely wrong.In one of the absolute stupidest, self-sabotaging booking decisions we've seen in quite some time, WWE booked a triple-threat match — a match type notorious for having a no-DQ element to it — to end via a no-contest. That's right. Make that make sense.All it took for Kevin Owens vs. Gunther vs. Finn Balor to end without a winner was apparently Sami Zayn attacking two referees. (Fun fact: WWE has a quite a few more referees than that working for them.)In what world should that end a match? A match where the winner gets a world title shot, no less. Did "SmackDown" general manager Nick Aldis go home before the main event? Was he still hanging out with Danhausen? Were all the other referees or officials of any kind distracted in catering? This was seriously awful.SAMI 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8npQDGKhl7— WWE (@WWE) August 29, 2026 And it's a shame the ending was so bad, because the match itself had a high pace and was a great time between the ropes. But clearly, Zayn is dealing with a real hand injury, which has delayed WWE's desired progression of his story beat. He hasn't wrestled since SummerSlam — which was literally this same match but without him in it.Honestly, I shouldn't even have to describe why this was all so dumb.The only good bit of continuity out of all this was Owens' interaction with Randy Orton backstage.A friendship that needs to be workshopped 😂@FightOwensFight | @RandyOrton pic.twitter.com/pxPucduYFH— WWE (@WWE) August 29, 2026 Getting personalSpeaking of Orton, he and Cody Rhodes went face-to-face in an intense promo battle. It was good, purely thanks to each man digging deep with the family insults. Other than that, it didn't really add much to their feud."Are you at a crossroads" 😳@RandyOrton | @CodyRhodes pic.twitter.com/knmt9mDl1b— WWE (@WWE) August 29, 2026 Nobody plays mind games like The Viper 🐍@RandyOrton pic.twitter.com/HSWJSJpGeF— WWE (@WWE) August 29, 2026 It's about to be a WAR when @CodyRhodes battles @RandyOrton at #SNME! 👊 pic.twitter.com/0d0TUq3mrF— WWE (@WWE) August 29, 2026 WWE booked itself into somewhat of a corner by adding the "you can't touch each other unless you want to never challenge for a world title again" stipulation to this. It feels wildly familiar in some respects and can be really exploited by Orton in particular. Have him go a step further by actually getting Rhodes' family involved. It's not like we haven't seen that type of personal depth in WWE storylines countless times over the years, after all.The "SmackDown" SquabblesBlack and blue. I see what WWE is doing with Chelsea Green by having her do nothing but lose since winning the interim world title. I really do. It's going to build to a "big," happy, first successful title defense. (Hopefully.) But it just feels wrong, and it isn't establishing her as the caliber she should be treated as. The woman is wicked over. Pay. It. articles.title: Comedian finds the secret to surviving boomer parents: Put them in your act
articles.summary: Jared Freid's Netflix special "Family Plan" explores the chaotic dynamic between millennials and their boomer parents, starting with one question asked on vacation.
articles.body: "How much do you weigh?" This question, asked of comedian Jared Freid by his father while on vacation in Delray Beach, Florida, became the inspiration for his new hour of stand-up covering family, body issues, adulthood and the strange closeness between millennials and their boomer parents. He also justifies why, at 41 years old, he chooses to remain on the family cellphone plan. Aptly titled "Family Plan," Freid's second special will drop on Netflix Sept. 1. The comic is known for giving dating advice on his long-running podcasts, "The JTrain Podcast" and "U Up?" and most recently in his new book, "Walking Red Flag." Freid sat down with Fox News Digital to talk about his new special and unpack his parental relationships, from some of his "most horrific memories" involving his mother arguing with other moms over beach chairs to the grave realization that he has the exact same body as his father. For all his jesting complaints about his loud, Jewish family, Freid described them as "the main driver" of his material. Frustration is where a lot of his jokes originate, he said, and few people frustrate him with as much precision as his own kin. "We [millennials] have a weird relationship, that's okay to acknowledge, with our parents," Freid said. B.Y.O. Boomer: Fun for the whole family "Millennials are incredibly insecure and notice everything. Boomers are incredibly confident and unaware. And what a horrible combination," the comedian said. "Millennials might be living in hell on earth, considering that combination. Our parents are the most confident and unaware generation, and we have to deal with them every day and we love them," he continued. "So that takes an incredible amount of restraint and empathy from our end, because the enraging part about parents is they're always 10% right." Freid, who clarified that he uses the word "boomer" with love, made the case that millennials have a uniquely intertwined relationship with their parents, in part because many millennials are worse off financially than the generation before them, which comes with certain entanglements (like staying on the family phone plan or attending a family vacation paid for by mom and dad). JEFF ARCURI REVEALS HOW 'BACHELORETTE' WIFE’S CANCER FIGHT TRANSFORMED HIS COMEDY — AND THEIR MARRIAGE He said "Family Plan" is exactly the type of comedy he wants to do: an hour of material, unified by the through-line of the Freid family beach trip, that people can watch with their own families, be it their parents or "that cousin that they go and smoke weed with during Thanksgiving." That approach has already shaped his next hour. Freid said his current material grew from another parental indignity: his father offering him Ozempic at dinner. "Should I be embarrassed to leave the house? Do I look that horrific that you have to offer me your prescription medication?" Freid wondered. Rather than repeat the jokes from "Family Plan" — Freid made it clear that his parents provide no shortage of material — he will try to repeat its form, starting with a moment of anger and letting it expand into something larger. I'll be your mirror The specifics of the set are his, but the emotional dynamic is widely recognizable, and fans have told him so. "People would come up to me and go, 'That's my parents! You're talking about my dad, that's my mom. My parents ask me about my weight and are obsessed with my body and I'm on the family plan.'" Beyond merely cracking jokes at boomers' expense, Freid aims to create a humorous mirror that allows audiences to recognize their own loved ones. He is careful about where he points the joke. "I only talk about myself," he said. "I want to make fun of people I know and love." COMEDIAN DES BISHOP ON HOW AMERICA MADE HIM FUNNIER AND HIS 'HEALTHY COLLABORATION' WITH WIFE HANNAH BERNER His material seems to resonate especially powerfully with Jewish crowds. "I have Jews come up to me, and they go, 'Does anyone else get it?' And I'm like, 'You were in the room, everyone was laughing!'" he said. "Being Jewish, to me, is a culture of discussion and love and empathy and [getting] annoyed, and all of those things. And that's all in this... I do believe stand-up is our Jewish sport, you know? We created the art form. When I do shows for Jews, I'm representing the whole culture." The boomer-parent material is contemporary, but Freid sees himself working inside a much older tradition of turning aggravation into laughter. And it doesn't stop at his own family. The Atkins Diet Freid performs an extended bit in "Family Plan" roasting Rob Lowe for serving as the face of Atkins, a pairing he found especially absurd as someone who has struggled with body issues himself. "There is nothing as transparent as we're gonna put Rob Lowe in our commercial so that chubby me will believe that if I eat Atkins foods, I can become Rob Lowe," Freid told Fox News Digital. Then he actually met Lowe. Freid encountered the actor at a Netflix golf tournament and nervously introduced himself, explaining that he had been doing a joke about him onstage every night for two years. Lowe immediately knew which one. "Atkins?" Freid recalled him saying. "I heard about the bit. I heard it's hilarious. Can't wait to see it." DAVID CROSS DOESN’T 'GIVE A F---’: THE ACTOR-COMEDIAN ON HIS NEW SPECIAL, SOCIAL MEDIA AND ‘TERRIFYING’ AI "I melted," Freid said. The moment forced Freid to live up to his own self-imposed standards of conduct. "I only make fun of people I could meet," he said. 'Stand-up is the love of my life.' (Don't tell his girlfriend.) Freid made it this far on his own terms. He said Hollywood never regarded him as an obvious star. "No one was going to come knock on my door to say, 'Jared, you got the goods. You're so good looking, we need to put you on TV.'" NATE BARGATZE REVEALS FAMILY-FOCUSED VISION BEHIND $350M NASHVILLE THEME PARK AHEAD OF HIS FIRST MOVIE RELEASE That forced him to build direct relationships with audiences through podcasts, social media, books and touring. He's been pursuing stand-up for 16 years, describing it as the love of his life. Everything else has been in service of making it into a career. "That's why I do a lot. You know, two podcasts, and the book, and stand-up. It's always been like a little bit of a desperation," Freid laughed. The comic graduated from Penn State with a degree in economics before moving to New York City. He thought he would sell insurance and annuities, but it wasn't for him. The best part of his day was writing emails, he said. Specifically, he enjoyed making friends and colleagues laugh on group email threads or over Google Chat. "It made me feel amazing, so I was like, 'How do I do that all the time? How do I take that drug?' And that turned into me doing open mics and sketch class and improv class and eventually, you know, becoming a comedian." Nobody has it figured out Freid, known for dishing dating advice, has this year entered a relationship of his own. Asked if his position as a prominent voice in the online dating discussion creates any pressure to have his own situation figured out, Freid replied simply, "No." "I don't think good advice comes from people who have it figured out. I think good advice come from vulnerability and admitting your faults," he explained. DAN GAINOR: GEN Z IS RIGHT TO BE ANGRY, BUT BOOMERS ARE NOT THE REAL ENEMY The instinct to carve his own path and be authentic carries over from his comedy philosophy into his dating work and new book, which he named after himself. "It's called 'Walking Red Flag' because I'm the red flag. I'm not trying to be a hero. I'm telling you how I felt, the emotional things I was going through, because I am 10% away from any guy someone's dating." He warned against trusting people who market themselves as finished products. "If anyone says they've figured it out, they're a liar trying to make money off you." For better or worse, Freid has people in his life who have no problem pointing out his perceived flaws. There's no stopping Jewish mothers For all the frustration Freid mines from his family, he doesn’t seem particularly interested in escaping it. Asked what advice he would give Jewish mothers whose sons have started dating, Freid laughed off the premise. "They're not going to listen to me," he said. "Keep bothering your sons. Keep giving them crap. They love you for it," Freid continued. "It actually calms them." FROM SOUTHERN CLUBS TO NETFLIX: HOW CLEAN COMIC DERRICK STROUP IS STOPPING AUDIENCES IN THEIR TRACKS He described the familiar barrage from his own mother: When are you coming home? When are you leaving? Why are you eating that? Eat, you haven’t eaten anything. Stop eating. Take. Eat. Drink. What are you drinking for? You drive so fast. You drive like an old lady. For Freid, that running commentary is less a nuisance to be solved than a kind of family soundtrack. "That is like a Jewish man’s white noise machine," he joked. Fortunately, it is also an endless source of material. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP After 16 years in stand-up, Freid has learned that the people who can get under his skin most effectively are often the same people who make for his best stories. His parents may never stop asking questions, offering opinions or telling him what he should be doing differently. At this point, Freid probably wouldn’t want them to.

articles.title: Little League World Series championship 2026: Curaçao wins second LLWS title with 11-2 win over Henderson, Nevada
articles.summary: Curaçao wins the LLWS for the second time since 2004, putting the game out of reach on Juriënsly De Windt's 3-run double.
articles.body: Curaçao won the 2026 Little League World Series championship with an 11-2 win over Henderson, Nevada, (representing the U.S. Mountain region) before an estimated crowd of 24,844 at Howard J. Lamade Stadium in Williamsport, Pennsylvania, on Sunday. Juriënsly De Windt hit a bases-loaded double to clear the bases and drive in three runs in the top of the fifth inning to blow open a game that was still in reach for Nevada at the beginning of the frame, trailing 4-2.Prior to De Windt's decisive blow, Nevada pitcher Logan Edwards loaded the bases on a Steven Felix single, Jaymiel Antonia double and intentional walk to Nathanael Jansen. The right-hander struck out the next two batters and looked like he might escape the jam with minimal damage. Curazao se pone aún más cerca del campeonato de la Serie Mundial de Pequeñas Ligas con doblete productor de tres carreras 🇨🇼👏.Lo ganan por 6 y están a 6 outs del campeonato 🔥. pic.twitter.com/zZq149Zmko— ESPN Béisbol ⚾️ (@ESPN_Beisbol) August 30, 2026 But Edwards then hit Shardijon De Lanoi with a pitch to put Curaçao ahead 5-2.With an 8-2 lead in the sixth, Curaçao added two more runs after loading the bases on singles from Zha-djir Janga and Giendry Ryan, followed by a walk by Naeem Angel Coeriel. Pitcher Brooks McFarland threw a wild pitch, allowing Janga to score. Then V-dien Ignacio Lindo dropped a bunt to third base to score a run on a fielder's choice and increase Curaçao's lead to eight runs. THE MOMENT CURAÇAO WON ITS FIRST LLWS CHAMPIONSHIP SINCE 2004 🔥🏆 pic.twitter.com/Aq86I5cGJE— SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) August 30, 2026 Nevada showed some life in the bottom of the sixth with consecutive one-out walks by Owen Guzman and James Esbar. Curaçao then changed pitchers from Giendry Ryan tp Steven Felix. He then hit Hudson Cowley with a pitch to load the bases.But Felix recovered to strike out Brooks McFarland on a curveball and got Jace Ward to fly out to close out the championship win.ESPN's Karl Ravech calls final LLWS championshipESPN broadcaster Karl Ravech called his last LLWS championship on Sunday after the network laid him off just over a month ago. Ravech has called 20 consecutive Little League World Series. "This event, more than anything else, is my thing," Ravech said to the Washington Post's Noah White. "I love this place. And I think most people recognize me because of this."The LLWS and ESPN paid tribute to Ravech on-air with Eduardo Perez, Jessica Mendoza and Todd Frazier presenting him with a photo during the telecast. ESPN honors Karl Ravech during his final broadcast of the Little League World Seriespic.twitter.com/18utRzclyO— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) August 30, 2026 Consolation Game: Japan 3, Ohio 2In the third-place game played earlier on Sunday, Japan rallied for three runs in the sixth for a walk-off 3-2 win over Hamilton, Ohio (representing the U.S. Great Lakes region).Xander Kinkade's two-run double in the fourth inning off Tensei Yazawa scored Josiah Infante and Bob Frazier gave Ohio a 2-0 lead.A WALK-OFF BUNT FOR JAPAN TO COME BACK AND WIN IT 🇯🇵🔥Japan is your third-place winner of the Little League World Series! 🥉 pic.twitter.com/yc1rARR4Bb— ESPN (@espn) August 30, 2026 But Japan led off the sixth with singles from Shinnosuke Ijima and Hiroto Yokote. With one out, Sou Koyama drove in Ijima. Following a Ryoji Sasaki strikeout, Ayumu Hasegawa dropped a bunt down the first-base line that Caiden Trent could not field and Koyama scored the game-winner.The LLWS schedule and results leading up to Sunday's championship game can be seen here.Here is how the 2026 Little League World Series championship played out with updates and highlights from Yahoo Sports' live blog of the game:

articles.title: Hasan Piker insists Abdul El-Sayed asked him to 'stump' for Michigan campaign amid backlash
articles.summary: Hasan Piker claimed Abdul El-Sayed asked him to stump for his Michigan U.S. Senate campaign before the Twitch streamer faced intense political backlash.
articles.body: Twitch streamer Hasan Piker said that Democratic Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed asked him to "stump" for his campaign during an interview Friday following the intense backlash the Democratic politician has faced for appearing with him. Piker spoke to Semafor columnist David Weigel about the backlash he has received from Democrats since appearing on the campaign trail with El-Sayed, which he claimed was El-Sayed's idea, not his. "He asked me to stump for him, and I had not considered that ever before," Piker said. "I'd never really delivered a speech like that before." EL-SAYED PALS AROUND WITH FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER THE DAY BEFORE CRUCIAL MICHIGAN SENATE ELECTION Piker added that he had previously decided to get more involved with politics through New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's campaign but did not face significant backlash for that effort compared to campaigning for El-Sayed. He explained that after campaigning for El-Sayed, establishment Democrats and think tanks like Third Way came out to attack him. "I'll admit I didn't realize how much the media would think that this is different," he continued. "I had no idea that in the mindset of, you know, people in D.C., in the mindset of like, establishment media, doing a rally with a politician was apparently far more consequential than flying out to Dearborn and, like, working out with him, doing profiles, fundraising for him. I didn't realize that it was a very different thing," Piker said. He continued, "I did not realize that people would get so mad about it because, from my perspective, who cares if I'm doing a rally with a politician? I'm like, I've already had the guy on, like, a hundred times on the broadcast. You know, I've fundraised for him. I like him a lot. I have my disagreements with him, too, of course. But that was when the onslaught came in." ABDUL EL-SAYED PLAYS DOWN HASAN PIKER TIES AFTER STREAMER’S VIRAL ANTISEMITISM FIRESTORM Fox News Digital reached out to El-Sayed's campaign for comment. El-Sayed has received intense scrutiny for campaigning with Piker despite the far-left Twitch streamer's history of controversial statements, such as claiming America "deserved" 9/11. More recently, El-Sayed has attempted to distance himself from Piker after he suggested Jewish Americans were "making antisemitism worse" by voicing their support of Israel. El-Sayed has since repeatedly referred to Piker as "a streamer from California" with no relevancy to the race. "I am not interested in a conversation about a social media person in California. And to folks who want to make this about a social media person in California, let’s not forget what actually matters in our politics, what our politics are really about," El-Sayed told reporters during Saturday's state Democratic Party Nominating Convention. MICHIGAN DEMOCRAT DEMANDS REPORTERS STOP ASKING 'ABOUT HASAN PIKER' AHEAD OF SENATE RACE He added, "I don’t ever want my comments to hurt anybody’s feelings. It’s important to me that people understand that I take serious [sic] the pain of all communities in this state. But I don’t want to have a conversation about a Twitch streamer in California. This is not a serious conversation." In a comment to Fox News Digital, El-Sayed also apologized for his past comments made in response to an attack on a Michigan synagogue in March, where he remarked, "Hurt people, hurt people." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "To anybody who feels like my comments may have been hurtful, I’m really sorry. That was not my intention. We condemned that terrorist attack. We condemned it outright," El-Sayed told Fox News Digital. "What I was trying to do was offer context for why it happened, but it wasn’t the time for context and you don’t ever want to trample somebody’s pain."

articles.title: Amazon makes Alexa+ free on compatible Fire TVs
articles.summary: Amazon's Alexa+ rolls out free to Fire TV devices across the U.S., but hands-free microphones and stored voice data raise key privacy questions.
articles.body: AI is coming to your TV, and if you own a compatible Fire TV, Amazon may add it without you doing anything. Amazon is rolling out Alexa+ to compatible Fire TV devices across the U.S. at no additional cost. You do not need an Amazon Prime membership for the Fire TV experience. There is no app to download or subscription to activate either. Eligible devices get upgraded automatically. That means millions of televisions and streaming devices are gaining a more conversational AI assistant. But what you probably really want to know is: What can you actually say to it? There is also a privacy question worth answering. Some Fire TV devices have hands-free microphones while others rely on the microphone button on the remote. Alexa also stores information about your interactions depending on your settings. So, here is how to try Alexa+ on your Fire TV and how to check the controls behind it. Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our financial protection checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed. Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com ALEXA+ LETS YOU ORDER FOOD LIKE A REAL CONVERSATION What Alexa+ changes on your Fire TV The old Alexa worked best when you gave it a fairly direct command. Alexa+ can understand more natural conversations and follow-up questions. For example, you can describe the kind of movie you want rather than knowing its title. Then you can narrow the results without repeating your entire request. Amazon says Alexa+ users are having nearly twice as many conversations on Fire TV compared with the original Alexa. The company also says viewers choose Alexa's top movie recommendation more than 40% more often than they did previously. The assistant reaches beyond entertainment too. It can interact with compatible smart home devices and display supported camera feeds. You can also ask general questions while you watch TV. How to start using Alexa+ on Fire TV How you talk to Alexa+ depends on the Fire TV hardware you have. If you use a Fire TV Stick: Press and hold the Alexa or microphone button on your Alexa Voice Remote. Say what you want, then release the button. Amazon says current Fire TV Sticks use the remote for voice control. Hands-free control requires a linked Echo device. If you use a Fire TV Cube: You can press the microphone button on the remote or speak to Alexa from across the room. The current Fire TV Cube supports native hands-free Alexa through its built-in microphone array. If Alexa is built into your smart TV: Capabilities vary by model. Some supported televisions have hands-free Alexa while others rely on the voice remote or a linked Echo. Amazon's device specifications identify which models support far-field voice control. Once Alexa+ appears on your Fire TV, there is no special Alexa+ mode you need to open. Just start talking to it. Try these Alexa+ commands on your Fire TV The real fun starts when you stop treating Alexa like a search box. Try conversational requests and follow up naturally. Some features depend on the streaming service, your subscriptions and the smart home devices connected to Alexa. Amazon specifically highlights conversational entertainment searches, follow-up questions, Ring camera feeds, smart home controls and general information requests as part of Alexa+ on Fire TV. It also supports jumping directly to described scenes in thousands of Prime Video movies. That last feature may be especially useful when you are trying to find one memorable moment without dragging the progress bar back and forth. CHEAP STREAMING BOX COULD HIJACK YOUR HOME INTERNET Amazon products that work well with the new Alexa+ experience If your current television still works perfectly, a streaming stick may be the easiest way to add the newer Fire TV experience. For an affordable upgrade: Fire TV Stick HD Amazon's latest Fire TV Stick HD supports Wi-Fi 6 and includes voice control through the Fire TV remote. It is designed for HD streaming and can also work with a linked Echo for hands-free Alexa control. For a 4K television: Fire TV Stick 4K Plus The Fire TV Stick 4K Plus supports 4K Ultra HD, Dolby Vision, HDR10+ and Dolby Atmos. It includes an Alexa Voice Remote. Like the other current sticks, hands-free Alexa requires a linked Echo. For hands-free Alexa: Fire TV Cube The Fire TV Cube makes the most sense if you specifically want to speak to Alexa without reaching for the remote. Amazon's current Cube has a four-microphone array and supports native hands-free Alexa. To compare these Fire TV options and find links to the models we recommend, visit CyberGuy.com. Is your Fire TV microphone always listening? This is where the type of Fire TV you own makes a big difference. If you have a Fire TV Stick, the streaming stick itself does not provide native hands-free Alexa. You normally press the microphone button on the Alexa Voice Remote when you want to speak. Amazon says a blue indicator appears on the television when the remote is recording your request and sending it to the cloud. If you pair that Fire TV Stick with an Echo, the Echo can provide hands-free voice control. The Fire TV Cube works differently. It has built-in microphones designed to hear the Alexa wake word from across the room. Amazon says supported hands-free Fire TV devices use on-device wake-word detection. Once the device recognizes the wake word, audio is sent to Amazon's cloud for processing. Amazon says that audio can include a fraction of a second from immediately before the wake word. That is worth knowing before you start using Alexa+ heavily. How to physically turn off a hands-free Fire TV microphone If your Fire TV device supports hands-free Alexa, look for its microphone-off button or switch. Amazon says using that control disconnects power to the microphones. A red light appears to show that the microphones are disabled. With the microphones off, that device cannot record or stream audio when you say the Alexa wake word. You can still use an Alexa Voice Remote because the remote has its own microphone that activates when you press its voice button. That gives you a useful middle ground. You can disable hands-free listening while keeping voice commands available whenever you intentionally press the remote button. Turn off Alexa Follow Up Mode if you want less listening Alexa can support follow-up requests so you do not have to repeat the wake word every time. If you prefer Alexa to stop listening after each request, Amazon says you can disable Follow Up Mode in your device settings or through the Alexa app. There is an even easier option. Say: "Alexa, turn off Follow Up Mode." Amazon confirms that voice command can disable the feature. Check what Alexa has saved about you If you are going to use Alexa+ more often, I would spend a minute looking at your Alexa history. Here you can review voice recordings, transcripts and typed Alexa requests associated with your Amazon account. Amazon says you can also delete them. Amazon provides controls here for managing how your voice recordings are retained and whether they can be used to improve its services. If you use Alexa to control lights, cameras or other connected equipment, check More > Alexa Privacy > Manage Your Alexa Data > Smart Home Device History as well. Amazon says you can delete that history or have certain smart home information automatically deleted after three or 18 months. Keep in mind that deleting Alexa history may affect personalization and certain Alexa features. NEW AMAZON AI SEARCH TURNS WORDS INTO SHOPPABLE IMAGES Check these privacy controls directly on Fire TV too Alexa privacy is only one part of the equation. Fire TV has its own data settings. Amazon notes that turning these settings off does not stop every form of data collection. Some device information still gets processed to provide features, troubleshoot problems and operate Amazon services. Apps such as Prime Video may have separate privacy controls too. These settings are device-specific. If you have more than one Fire TV in the house, Amazon says you need to review the settings on each one. What Alexa+ costs now Here is an important detail that could easily get lost in the word "free." Compatible Fire TV owners in the U.S. can now use many Alexa+ features on their television at no additional charge, regardless of whether they have Prime. However, Amazon still charges $19.99 a month for its broader Alexa+ Standard Plan for non-Prime members. Prime members receive the broader Alexa+ experience as part of Prime. Prime or the Alexa+ Standard Plan also unlocks additional capabilities. Amazon lists Alexa Routines, access to specific Ring camera moments and advanced Home Modes among the extra Fire TV features. Subscribers also get Alexa+ on compatible Echo devices. So, you can get plenty of Alexa+ functionality on a compatible Fire TV without paying another monthly fee. Just do not assume every Alexa+ feature across every Amazon device has become free. What this means to you For most Fire TV owners, the biggest improvement will probably be search. Scrolling through endless rows of movies can get old fast. Being able to describe what you want and then refine the results by talking naturally could make Alexa+ genuinely useful. Smart home controls add another layer. If you already use Ring cameras, compatible lights or connected locks, the television becomes another place to manage them. The automatic upgrade deserves attention too. You may suddenly have an AI assistant with new capabilities on a device you have owned for years. That makes this a good time to understand whether your particular Fire TV has hands-free microphones and review the privacy choices connected to Alexa. You can use the convenience without leaving every data setting untouched. Kurt's key takeaways I like the direction Amazon is taking with Alexa+ on Fire TV because voice search badly needed an upgrade. Asking for a movie the way you would describe it to a friend feels far more useful than remembering an exact title. The hands-on features are where this gets interesting. I can see myself asking about an actor while watching a movie or pulling up a front-door camera without reaching for my phone. Still, an automatic AI upgrade should also trigger an automatic privacy check in your head. First, find out where the microphone actually lives. A Fire TV Stick's remote works differently from the hands-free microphones in a Fire TV Cube. Then look through Alexa Privacy and the Fire TV Privacy Settings menu. You may decide you are comfortable with everything exactly as Amazon configured it. You may also find a few switches you would rather change. Either way, that choice should belong to you. Would you rather have Alexa+ automatically added to your Fire TV, or should Amazon make AI features like this something you choose to turn on yourself? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com.
